q1: SELECT f1.drinker, f2.drinker FROM (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f1, (SELECT drinker, SUM(times_a_week) AS st FROM frequents GROUP BY drinker) AS f2 WHERE f1.drinker < f2.drinker AND f1.st = f2.st
q2: SELECT DISTINCT drinker AS drinkerA, drinkerB FROM frequents JOIN (SELECT drinker AS drinkerB, times_a_week FROM frequents) AS frequentsB ON frequents.times_a_week < frequentsB.times_a_week

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 compares the total times a week each drinker frequents any bar, while Q2 checks if there are any two drinkers where one frequents a bar more times a week than the other.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have at least two drinkers, each frequenting the same bar, but with different frequencies. The condition that triggers the difference is when the frequency of one drinker is greater than the other for the same bar.
